# Results — Study 452 (Spinning-Top)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a spinning
top (small body, two long comparable wicks) marks indecision that resolves into a directional
move** — encoded as a mechanical rule. A bar is a spinning top iff its body is `< 25%` of the
day's range, both wicks are `≥ 25%` of the range, and the two wicks are comparable (the smaller
is `≥ 50%` of the larger). The pattern is read on the close of `t`; the long is entered at the
**next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes/OHLC for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **3006** mechanical spinning tops pooled across the 5 tapes (body<25%, wicks≥25%, balance≥0.5) |
| Timing / costs | pattern read on close of `t`; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per entry |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. This is a single-instrument event study, not a cross-sectional
> anomaly, so survivorship affects only the drift baseline (which the random-entry control
> neutralizes). Candle bodies/wicks are taken from the adjusted OHLC, the same tape every chart
> package would display.

## The signal — spinning-top vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch top-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = top − random. **The Welch *t* and the
random baseline are averaged over 20 random-baseline seeds** — a single lucky draw of random
dates is not evidence, so we report the seed-robust mean and its `[min, max]` spread.

| horizon | n | top | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (top−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* (mean) | Welch *t* [min,max] |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 3003 | +23.4 bps | 59% | +4.50 | +23.9 bps | **−0.5 bps** | +21.4 bps | −0.07 | [−1.15, +0.82] |
| 10-day | 2995 | +57.9 bps | 61% | +6.83 | +48.6 bps | **+9.3 bps** | +55.9 bps | +1.02 | [−0.01, +2.39] |
| 20-day | 2988 | +120.3 bps | 64% | +8.35 | +97.7 bps | **+22.7 bps** | +118.3 bps | +1.73 | [+0.67, +3.38] |
| 60-day | 2963 | +292.4 bps | 70% | +8.46 | +296.6 bps | **−4.2 bps** | +290.4 bps | −0.20 | [−2.07, +1.16] |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+8.35** at 20 days) —
but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit the drift.
Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the spinning top adds at most **+22.7 bps** (20d)
and is flat-to-negative at 5/60d. Crucially, the touch-minus-random Welch *t* **never clears the
desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar on average** (max mean +1.73 at 20d). A *single* random-date draw can land as
high as +3.38 at 20d — but the same horizon ranges down to +0.67 across seeds, so the >2
readings are **luck in the choice of comparison dates**, not a robust edge. Indecision does not
forecast direction.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent cross-sectional edge

| ticker | entries | top | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (top−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 639 | +111.8 bps | +3.87 | +74.3 bps | **+37.5 bps** |
| QQQ | 549 | +168.3 bps | +4.77 | +84.4 bps | **+83.8 bps** |
| IWM | 536 | +130.2 bps | +3.52 | +35.7 bps | **+94.5 bps** |
| DIA | 656 | +94.6 bps | +3.65 | +98.7 bps | **−4.1 bps** |
| GLD | 626 | +105.7 bps | +3.28 | +96.3 bps | **+9.3 bps** |

The single-seed (seed=7) per-ticker deltas look positive in 4 of 5 names — but they ride almost
entirely on QQQ and IWM (the two highest-vol baskets, where random dates happen to land on
weaker windows for *this* seed), and DIA is already negative. Re-draw the random dates and the
pooled gap collapses below the *t* = 2 bar (see the seed spread above). No stable, broad edge.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the wicks, almost nothing changes

The decisive "does the *shape* matter?" test: keep each bar's open/close (so the price path and
body sizes are untouched) but **shuffle the two wick lengths across bars**, destroying the
small-body/balanced-wick geometry while preserving the marginal wick distribution. If price
genuinely respected *the spinning-top shape*, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed top 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY wick-scramble | +111.8 bps | **0.066** | 500 |

About **7% of scrambled-geometry candles match or beat the real spinning top** (*p* = 0.066,
stable at ~0.07 with 2000 draws). That is **above the 0.05 bar** — the specific small-body /
balanced-wick shape is *not* load-bearing at conventional significance: a random re-pairing of
wicks does nearly as well, because what little the rule picks up is "a high-range, two-sided
day" (an elevated-volatility flag), not the spinning-top geometry per se. "Indecision forecasts
direction" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real resolution

On a deterministic tape where a spinning-top day is *planted* to be followed by a real upward
burst (knob `edge`), the same rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a
genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | top | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no resolution) | 713 | −47.5 bps | 47% | −1.45 |
| **1.20** (real planted resolution) | 704 | +246.6 bps | 70% | **+7.38** |

With no planted resolution the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 / slightly negative (no false positive); a
real planted resolution lights up at *t* = +7.38 with a 70% win-rate. The detector is live — so
the flat real-tape result is an honest null.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The spinning top does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline: the
  top-minus-random Welch *t* never clears 2 on average (−0.07 / +1.02 / +1.73 / −0.20 at
  5/10/20/60 days). The lone >2 readings are a lucky draw of random comparison dates (the 20d
  Welch ranges +0.67 → +3.38 across seeds). The huge one-sample *t*'s (20d +8.35) are pure beta —
  the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No residual edge once the free drift is removed, and costs only
  deepen the hole. You'd capture the same drift more cheaply by **holding the index**; a rule
  that fires only on indecision candles trades less and pays costs on each. Nothing to scale.
- **"Does indecision forecast direction"? — BUSTED.** The wick-scramble placebo leaves the
  result essentially intact (*p* = 0.07): geometric-nonsense candles do nearly as well as real
  spinning tops, so the small-body/balanced-wick *shape* carries no usable forecasting
  information. The spinning top is a descriptive label for a quiet, two-sided day, not a forecast.
